Hi Ethan —

Great to hear this is moving. Below is a pragmatic checklist we've used for similar ISV co-sells and cloud marketplace listings (AWS/GCP/Azure):

1) Compliance & security evidence
- SOC 2 Type II (summary + report)
- Pen test summary and any remediation notes
- Data residency statement + key management (KMS/HSM) notes
2) Product & Ops artifacts
- Product overview (200–400 words) + feature bullets for offer page
- SKU/entitlement mapping and metering schema (how you want to bill: per inference-hour, token-based, seat, etc.)
- SLA summary and uptime targets for hosted vs private deployments
3) Technical evidence
- Network diagram for hosted and private deployments
- API/ingress whitelist instructions for private link or VPC connections
- Telemetry/observability excerpt (what we'll provide during POC and in production)
4) Commercial & enablement
- Pricing table (list + suggested co-sell discount bands)
- Joint GTM one-pager + co-sell motion owner names
- Demo plan and contact for enablement sessions

I've attached our marketplace-evidence-template.xlsx and a short co-sell-playbook.pdf to this thread — those should help you structure materials so the listing and partner enablement teams can digest them quickly. A couple of notes specific to your questions:

- Private/on-prem offerings: you can list an offering that is deployable on-prem or via a private offer, but the listing must clearly indicate whether consumable via a managed hosted SKU, a private offer, or customer-managed on-prem. We typically add a "deployment options" section to the offer page.
- On metering: we recommend defining an explicit SKU for each billing unit (eg. "inference-hour", "embedding-100k-units"); Ben can call out a couple of gotchas for AWS metering.

Next steps: can you add the procurement contact and the internal Skyline owner for the co-sell motion? If possible, upload an initial draft to the Drive folder linked below and we'll do a sweep. I'm available Wed/Thu morning for a 30-minute align.

Thanks,

Adding a couple items from the metering/ops side so Skyline can shape the SKUs: 

- AWS/GCP favor discrete, immutable SKUs for billing reconciliation. If you plan both hosted and dedicated/reserved SKUs, label them clearly (eg. SKY-HOSTED-inference-hour, SKY-DEDICATED-reserved-hour).
- For private offers we need the seller account ID and the proposed pricing sheet up front so we can map to a private-offer SKU during listing authoring.
- Telemetry we need: per-tenant usage CSV fields (tenant_id, sku_id, usage_quantity, start_time, end_time). We can provide the template if you'd like.

HubSpot deal: I pulled the record and linked the draft to DEAL-1234567 so ops can track evidence handoff. Ethan — if you want me to own the metering mapping I'll take it (will need a short call with your engineering lead).

Ethan / team —

Quick technical clarifications from product side: 

- For on-prem/managed deployments: include a short install/runbook excerpt and any operator-level dependencies (eg. private endpoint, minimum GPU types, disk requirements). That helps the catalog reviewers mark the listing correctly.
- If you plan to offer an "air-gapped" or "govcloud" variant, call that out separately; the cert matrix is different and will slow the review.
- We've attached a sku-mapping.csv example to this thread that shows how we expect ids/patterns to be supplied for reconciliation.

Also, for the co-sell enablement deck: please include 2–3 representative TCO examples (customer size small/medium/large) so field sales can quickly recommend the right SKU. We can help generate those if you share expected usage profiles.

I'll be on the enablement call if we schedule one — happy to walk through the runbook and telemetry needs.

—Olga
